item.title: I did a thing.... First time published in The Lancet.
item.description: More importantly, our study showed proof of concept that minimally invasive cardiac surgery leads to better patient outcomes compared to traditional open-heart bypass surgery when performed at centres with surgeons and staff experienced in the procedure. Given that bypass surgery, or CABG, is the most performed cardiac surgery in the world, being able to perform the procedure without cutting a patient's breastbone is a big deal. Minimally invasive cardiac surgery can lead to fewer blood product transfusions, decreased risk of surgical wound infection, and reduced recovery time and pain experienced by patients. https://authors.elsevier.com/c/1nXO7V-4XWVpI #ClinicalResearch #CardiacSurgery
